concepts.learning_objective: Explain the dynamic nature of solid-liquid and liquid-vapour equilibria.
Relate equilibrium vapour pressure to the nature of a liquid and to temperature.
Apply Henry's law to equilibria involving dissolution of gases in liquids.

topics.title: Equilibrium in Chemical Processes and the Law of Chemical Equilibrium

concepts.learning_objective: Describe chemical equilibrium as dynamic and attainable from either direction.
Write Kc expressions and relate Kc values for reactions written differently.
Use Kp = Kc(RT)^delta-n for gaseous equilibria.
Write equilibrium constants for heterogeneous systems omitting pure solids and liquids.

topics.title: Applications of Equilibrium Constants and Relation with Gibbs Energy

concepts.learning_objective: Predict the extent of a reaction from the magnitude of K.
Predict the direction of a reaction by comparing Qc with Kc.
Use the relation delta-G standard = -RT ln K.
Apply Le Chatelier's principle to changes in concentration and pressure.
Predict how temperature changes K for exothermic and endothermic reactions.
Explain why a catalyst and an inert gas at constant volume do not shift equilibrium.
Identify Arrhenius, Bronsted-Lowry and Lewis acids and bases.
Calculate pH using the ionic product of water.
Calculate the degree of ionization and pH of weak acids.

topics.title: Hydrolysis of Salts and Buffer Solutions

concepts.learning_objective: Predict the pH of salt solutions from hydrolysis of their ions.
Describe buffers and calculate their pH with the Henderson-Hasselbalch equation.

topics.title: Solubility Equilibria of Sparingly Soluble Salts

concepts.learning_objective: Relate Ksp to molar solubility and predict precipitation.
Explain and calculate the common ion effect on solubility.
